newsitem.title: ITALY: BOXING-MAGISTRATES OPEN PROBE INTO BOXER'S DEATH.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-MAGISTRATES OPEN PROBE INTO BOXER'S DEATH.

text.p: Magistrates on Monday opened an inquiry into the death of middleweight boxer Fabrizio De Chiara after he collapsed at the end of an Italian title fight.
De Chiara, 25, fell into a coma following his 12-round contest against Vincenzo Imparato on Saturday. Doctors declared him dead less than 24 hours later.
Magistrates in the central town of Carrara, near where the fight took place, said they would study a video of the encounter and interview ringside spectators.
De Chiara's death brought renewed calls for boxing to be banned. "Yet another life has been swept away in the ring," the Vatican newspaper, L'Osservatore Romano wrote.
Saturday's fight was stopped mid-way through the 12th round after Imparato landed two sharp blows to De Chiara's head followed by one to the stomach, knocking him to the ground.

The referee ended the fight and the shaven-headed De Chiara made it back to his corner before collapsing. He was immediately taken to hospital, but died following two operations to remove blood that was putting pressure on his brain.
A devastated Imparato, who had lost to De Chiara in a previous encounter, said he thought Saturday's fight went on too long.
"The fight should have been stopped in the 11th round. I don't know why his trainer and manager didn't do this," Imparato said. "I saw that (De Chiara) was short of breath and exhausted," he added.
De Chiara's manager Mario Loreni said: "During the match
he was always lucid. I asked him 'can you do it?' and he always said 'yes'".
The Italian institute of civil rights on Monday urged the
government to impose a total ban on boxing until clear guidelines for the sport had been established.

"The problem of preventing risks and securing personal safety has never been properly addressed in Italy," said Maretta Scoca, chairwoman of the institute and a member of the centrist opposition party, the CCD.
The secretary general of the Italian Olympic Committee, Raffaele Pagnozzi, agreed that the rules governing boxing and ringside medical care needed to be reviewed.
"It might be a good idea to limit the number of fights to the bare minimum, to say that a boxer cannot take part in more than a certain number of fights in his career," Pagnozzi said.
Some newspapers called for boxing to be outlawed altogether.

"It's already doubtful whether on the threshold of the year 2000 two people should fight in a ring for money," wrote sports daily Tuttosport. "It is even more unacceptable that they should do it in unfavourable conditions, without protection and without any safety in hazardous situations," it added.
State broadcaster's RAI decision to show recorded film of the entire fight on Saturday night after people already knew that De Chiara was in intensive care, added to the controversy.
"The cynicism of man turned a drama into a macabre spectacle," L'Osservatore Romano said.

De Chiara was in Italy's 1992 Olympic boxing squad, losing in the first round of the superwelterweight competition. He turned professional two years ago and before Saturday's match had a record of 13 wins and one loss.
